page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.large is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

This instance includes 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, offering fast local read and write capabilities directly on the host. It also features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance is optimized for both network and Elastic Block Store (EBS) performance, making it suitable for workloads requiring consistent network throughput alongside local storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the m5dn.large sits in the lower performance tiers for intensive tasks. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is categorized as weak, while multi-core performance falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only large block speeds of 13.84 GB/sec and write speeds of 11.61 GB/sec, both in the bottom 10%. Geekbench single-core scores are average, but multi-core and application-specific benchmarks, such as software compilation and image processing, remain in the lower decile.

Given its hardware profile, the m5dn.large is qualitatively cost-efficient for entry-level general-purpose workloads that require local NVMe storage but do not demand high compute density. It is suitable for light database operations, basic web serving, small-scale development environments, and low-throughput background tasks.
